title: Fix the Method That Overloads Instead of Overrides
description: The program should have Dog override Animal's makeSound() method.
expectedBehavior: Calling makeSound() on a Dog (even through an Animal reference) should print 'Woof'.
actualProblem: Dog's makeSound(String extra) has a different parameter list than Animal's makeSound(), so it's an overload (a separate, new method), not an override. Calling a.makeSound() with no arguments still resolves to Animal's original version, printing '...' instead of anything dog-specific.
explanation: Overriding requires matching the parent method's name and parameter list exactly. A method with the same name but a different signature is a separate overload, not a replacement — adding @Override helps the compiler catch this mistake immediately.
